status_summary: Executive Order 14412 (signed 2026-06-22, published 2026-06-25) directs OMB guidance requiring agencies to move high-value assets and high-impact systems, excluding national security systems, to post-quantum cryptography for key establishment by 2030-12-31 and for digital signatures by 2031-12-31, and directs the NSA Director, as National Manager for National Security Systems, to report through the Committee on National Security Systems within 180 days (about 2026-12-19) and annually on migration status for national security systems. OMB's implementing Memorandum M-26-15 (2026-06-24) sets a five-phase schedule ending with full migration in 2035, a 2030-12-31 objective and agency plans due within 120 days, and does not apply to national security systems. Neither the order nor the memorandum revises National Security Memorandum 10's 2035 goal or names the intelligence community; Executive Order 14413 of the same date has the DNI and the Secretary of War identify national security implications of commercial quantum computing, including for post-quantum migration, with a report due within a year. ODNI's leadership page lists the IC Chief Information Officer among ODNI officials immediately after the Chief Operating Officer and the IC Chief Financial Officer, without a principal-staff label and without showing when that placement began.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14412 (Securing the Nation Against Advanced Cryptographic Attacks) was signed, setting post-quantum migration deadlines of 2030 and 2031 for non-national-security high-value and high-impact systems and a first NSA status report on national security systems due within 180 days (published in the Federal Register 2026-06-25).

Executive Order 14413 (Ushering in the Next Frontier of Quantum Innovation) was signed; section 4(f) has the DNI and the Secretary of War identify national security implications of commercial quantum computer scale, naming post-quantum cryptography migration as one (published 2026-06-25).

OMB issues Memorandum M-26-15, Execution of the Migration to Post-Quantum Cryptography, implementing Executive Order 14412: it sets five phases (planning 2026 to 2027, pilots 2027 to 2028, prioritized migration 2028 to 2030, signature migration 2031, full migration 2035), asks agencies to mitigate as much quantum risk as feasible by 2030-12-31, requires agency migration plans within 120 days and states that it does not apply to national security systems.

title: Make the IC CIO a DNI primary staff member; review post-quantum progress; revise 2035 goal
uncertainties: Both orders were read on the Federal Register; neither mentions NSM-10 or 2035. EO 14412's 2030 and 2031 deadlines for non-national-security systems are earlier than the 2035 goal, which is in line with the text's call to revise the goal, but the order does not revise the memorandum itself (an inference). Whether the NSA status report amounts to the Mandate's immediate review of IC and Defense progress is a judgment: it is a first report due six months after the order and about two years into the term. The leadership page does not label principal staff and does not list the General Counsel; the IC CIO's placement there may predate 2025, so it is not counted as an action. The cybersecurity order published in the Federal Register on 2025-06-11 was not checked for post-quantum text. Progress was lowered from 35 to 25 because the operative steps so far are directives and deadlines, with the review report not yet due. OMB Memorandum M-26-15 (2026-06-24) was read on whitehouse.gov; it excludes national security systems, mentions NSM-10 only in a footnote defining high-impact systems and names the Department of War only for shared cloud migration work, so it does not revise the 2035 goal for intelligence community or Defense systems. No ODNI, NSA or CNSS public action on national security system migration after June 2026 was found, and dni.gov was not reachable. Whether agencies submitted plans by the deadline of about 2026-10-22 was not found.
